items.title: git's –end-of-options Flag
items.raw_content: I was reading through the fix for a package manager CVE last week and ran into a git flag I’d somehow never noticed: --end-of-options . My first reaction was that some LLM had hallucinated it, but it’s documented in gitcli(7) , it was added in git 2.24.0 in November 2019, and it exists because git had already used -- for something else. In most Unix tools -- marks the end of option parsing, so rm -- -f removes a file called -f rather than passing the force flag. Git had repurposed -- early on to separate revisions from pathspecs, because git log foo on its own is ambiguous between a branch named foo and a file named foo and one of the two readings needed a marker: git log main -- README.md means commits on main touching that file. That left the revision position with no terminator, so if a script runs git log "$rev" and $rev starts with a dash, git parses it as an option.
items.title_zh: git 的 --end-of-options 标志
items.summary: A post explains git's little-known --end-of-options flag, added in git 2.24.0 in November 2019, which terminates option parsing for revisions because git had already repurposed -- to separate revisions from pathspecs.

items.title: Scaling Laws for Hypernetwork-Based Knowledge Injection in Large Language Models
items.title_zh: 基于超网络的大语言模型知识注入缩放定律
items.summary: The paper studies train-time factual knowledge injection by training a hypernetwork to generate a fixed LoRA adapter that lets the target model answer questions about a large fact corpus. Using a new MegaWikiQA dataset, it finds power-law scaling along hypernetwork depth, width, and target-model size, with reliable out-of-distribution generalization.

items.title: The Mechanism Matters: When Knowledge Graphs Help Reinforcement Learning
items.title_zh: 机制至关重要：知识图谱何时有助于强化学习
items.summary: A controlled study independently varies the RL task, the knowledge-graph injection mechanism (state features, action masking, or potential-based reward shaping), and graph quality in MiniGrid environments. It finds that structural KG guidance improves sample efficiency and solve reliability on compositional sparse-reward tasks, while hard action masking is brittle when the graph is incomplete or corrupted.

items.title: EGRNet: A Lightweight Semantic Segmentation Network with Edge-Gated Refinement and Adversarial Sensing
items.title_zh: EGRNet：结合边缘门控细化与对抗感知的轻量级语义分割网络
items.summary: EGRNet is a lightweight segmentation model for urban scenes that combines depthwise separable convolutions, dilated residual blocks, an edge-gated refinement module, and squeeze-and-excitation attention. With 0.46M parameters it reaches 65.28% mIoU on Cityscapes and adds a lightweight adversarial-attack detection strategy.

items.title: SCPP: A Unified Python Library for Soft Clustering
items.title_zh: SCPP：统一的软聚类 Python 库
items.summary: SCPP is an open-source Python framework that provides a scikit-learn-compatible estimator interface for soft clustering across fuzzy, probabilistic, graph-based, matrix-factorization, and deep learning methods. It integrates 40 algorithms together with benchmarking of clustering quality, runtime, memory, and scalability.

items.title: From Bit-Position Sensitivity to Unequal Error Protection for DNN Inference Memory
items.title_zh: 从比特位敏感性到 DNN 推理内存的不等错误保护
items.summary: The authors characterize per-bit-position fault sensitivity across 16 ML workloads and three floating-point formats, finding that low-order fraction bits are largely inconsequential while bits at the exponent-mantissa boundary cause catastrophic collapse. They derive per-data-type safe-bit floors and use them to design an unequal error protection codec that reduces ECC area and read energy.

items.title: HypEMBER: Hypernetwork-based Ensemble for Robust Policy Learning of Parametrized Dynamical Systems
items.title_zh: HypEMBER：面向参数化动力系统鲁棒策略学习的超网络集成方法
items.summary: HypEMBER combines hypernetworks with ensembling so that policy and value functions are conditioned on a system's physical parameters, enabling generalization across dynamical regimes. The ensemble quantifies epistemic uncertainty, and experiments on the Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation and a gyre-flow navigation task show improved training stability and robustness to measurement noise and parameter misspecification.
